title: Multiple-target tracing \(MTT) algorithm probes molecular dynamics at cell surface
protocol: Plate subconfluent cells on sterilized 18 mm round coverslips.
Allow cells to spread in the incubator overnight.
Dilute biotinylated antibody in culture medium supplemented with 100× biotin.
Mix diluted biotinylated antibody with equimolar amount of streptavidin-Qdots, typically at a concentration of 10 nM each.
Incubate the antibody-Qdot mixture for 15 min at 37°C.
Mount coverslips from the culture well in the observation chamber one at a time.
Incubate cells with the antibody-Qdot mix for 15 min at 37°C using culture medium supplemented with serum to prevent unspecific binding of Qdots to the coverslip.
Wash thoroughly three times with HBSS to remove unbound Qdots.
Image up to 30 min in 500 μl HBSS-Hepes on the microscope stage maintained at 37°C.
Warm the microscope stage and fluorescence lamp at least 1 h prior to measurements.
Select isolated and properly spread cells for imaging.
Perform a visual quality check with both transmitted and fluorescence illumination.
Acquire a DIC image of the cell before recording stacks.
Save the DIC image as TIFF with the same name as the subsequent stack(s).
Record stacks of single-molecule images using fluorescence microscopy setup.
Each stack consists of 300 images taken at 36 ms time-lag in full frame (512 x 512 pixels).
Acquire another DIC image after stack acquisition to check for photodamage.
Launch Octave or Matlab and add MTT code folders to the path.
Navigate to your data directory.
Adjust tracing parameters such as D_max by editing MTT_param.m if necessary.
Execute detect_reconnex_22.m script to start automatic analysis.
Read output data using scripts like fread_data_spt.m for further analyses.
